project.title: Shared equipment booking
project.subtitle: A delivery sequence that validates the booking flow before expanding it

phases.title: Prove the booking flow
phases.milestone: Five users complete a booking without assistance

phases.title: Run a controlled pilot
phases.milestone: One location manages real bookings for two weeks

phases.title: Make the service reliable
phases.milestone: Bookings can be restored and important incidents are visible

open_questions.text: Who may override or cancel another user’s booking?
How long should completed bookings remain searchable?

segments.title: Validate the core booking journey
segments.objective: Confirm that users understand availability and can complete a booking without assistance.
segments.summary: Test the central promise before building the full service.
deliverables: Anonymised report from five user sessions
acceptance: Five users understand the availability view
At least four complete a booking
risks: Test participants may be more comfortable with digital tools than the wider audience

segments.title: Deliver bookings for one location
segments.objective: Let authenticated users browse equipment, book a time slot and cancel their own booking.
segments.summary: Create the first usable end-to-end release.
acceptance: Two users cannot book the same equipment and time slot
risks: Unclear ownership rules may delay support decisions
questions: Should a pending booking expire automatically?

segments.title: Notify users of important changes
segments.objective: Keep users informed when a booking is created, changed or cancelled.
segments.summary: Reduce missed handovers during the pilot.
acceptance: Every booking change produces one clear notification
A notification never exposes another user’s private details
risks: Too many notifications may cause users to ignore them

segments.title: Protect and restore booking data
segments.objective: Make the pilot recoverable before adding more locations or users.
segments.summary: Add backup, restoration and essential monitoring.
acceptance: A backup restores into an isolated environment
A failed backup is visible to the operator
risks: A backup is not useful until restoration has been tested
questions: What recovery time is acceptable during the pilot?
